name: Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS), 14 items, U.S.-adapted wording
notes: Items and 1-point criteria are from the PREDIMED MEDAS (Schröder 2011). Thresholds were checked item by item against Table 1 of Martínez-González 2012 (PLoS One, open access), which reproduces the same validated 14-item questionnaire from the PREDIMED group; the Schröder 2011 full text was not reachable from this machine (abstract confirmed via PubMed/Europe PMC). Wording is adapted for U.S. foods; the adapted wording has NOT been separately validated. Questions are phrased so that 'yes' always earns the point (pointWhen = 'yes'); items 5, 6, 7 and 11 are reversed versions of the original 'how many' questions. Original serving sizes (grams) are kept.
validation: Schröder 2011: in 7,146 PREDIMED participants (older Spanish adults, 55-80 y, high cardiovascular risk), the MEDAS score correlated with an FFQ-derived score (r = 0.52; ICC 0.51) and with HDL-cholesterol, BMI, waist, triglycerides and glucose in the expected directions. Agreement was moderate (Bland-Altman limits 57-153%).

scoring.method: Sum 1 point per item answered 'yes' (pointWhen). Raw score and trend only.
scoring.cutoffNote: No validated cutoff exists for U.S. adults or for this adapted wording, so the app shows only the raw score and its trend. PREDIMED analyses grouped scores into categories (e.g., ≤5, 6-7, 8, 9, ≥10 in Martínez-González 2012) for research in older, high-risk Spanish adults; those are analysis categories, not validated 'good/poor adherence' thresholds, and are not used here.
scoring.nonDrinkerNote: Item 8 (wine) is scored for fidelity. Non-drinkers score 0 on it (maximum 13). This is expected and not a goal to change; compare a person's scores over time only.

evidenceNote: Validated screener (moderate agreement with a full FFQ) in older Spanish adults; the Mediterranean pattern it measures has strong trial evidence (PREDIMED). U.S. adaptation is unvalidated.

items.text: Is olive oil the main fat you cook with and add to food (instead of butter, margarine, or other oils)?
items.originalText: Do you use olive oil as main culinary fat?
items.yesCriterion: Yes = olive oil is the main culinary fat.
items.tip: Make olive oil your default: cook with it and use it instead of butter or margarine on bread and vegetables.
items.adaptationNote: Wording expanded to name common U.S. alternatives (butter, margarine, other oils); threshold unchanged.

items.text: Do you use 4 tablespoons or more of olive oil a day in total (cooking, salads, bread, and meals out)?
items.originalText: How much olive oil do you consume in a given day (including oil used for frying, salads, out-of-house meals, etc.)?
items.yesCriterion: Yes = ≥4 tablespoons/day (≈54 g; 1 tbsp olive oil = 13.5 g per USDA FDC).
items.tip: An easy way to add energy without extra bulk: drizzle olive oil on vegetables, beans, grains, eggs or bread.
items.adaptationNote: Threshold unchanged (≥4 tbsp). Note: 4 tbsp is ≈480 kcal (FDC) and above the prior DGA 2020-2025 Mediterranean-style pattern oil amounts (31-36 g/day at 2,400-2,800 kcal). Kept for scoring fidelity; for someone who undereats, olive oil is an energy-dense Mediterranean food (PREDIMED EVOO arm).

items.text: Do you eat 2 or more servings of vegetables a day, with at least one of them raw or as a salad? (1 serving ≈ 200 g, about a large side dish; a small side counts as half.)
items.originalText: How many vegetable servings do you consume per day? (1 serving: 200 g; consider side dishes as half a serving)
items.yesCriterion: Yes = ≥2 servings/day (1 serving = 200 g; side dishes count as ½), with ≥1 serving raw or as a salad.
items.tip: Add one vegetable side or a simple salad with olive oil to a meal you already eat.
items.adaptationNote: Serving kept at 200 g; described as 'about a large side dish' for U.S. users. Frozen and canned vegetables count (they are vegetables; DGA 2025-2030 lists all forms). Note this 200 g serving is larger than the U.S. cup-equivalent.

items.text: Do you eat 3 or more pieces of fruit a day? (1 piece = 1 medium fruit or about 1 cup of berries/grapes; 100% fruit juice counts in the original screener.)
items.originalText: How many fruit units (including natural fruit juices) do you consume per day?
items.yesCriterion: Yes = ≥3 fruit units/day (natural fruit juice counts in the original).
items.tip: Keep fruit where you'll see it, or pack a banana, apple or orange for the day.
items.adaptationNote: 'Fruit units' described with U.S. examples. Juice still counts for scoring fidelity, but app suggestions favor whole fruit because DGA 2025-2030 advises eating fruit in its original form and limiting 100% juice.

items.short: Red/processed meat under 1 serving a day
items.text: Do you eat red meat, burgers, or processed meats (ham, bacon, sausage, hot dogs, deli meat) less than once a day? (1 serving = 100-150 g, about 3.5-5 oz.)
items.originalText: How many servings of red meat, hamburger, or meat products (ham, sausage, etc.) do you consume per day? (1 serving: 100-150 g)
items.tip: Try swapping one deli-meat or burger meal this week for chicken, fish, beans or eggs.
items.adaptationNote: Question reversed so that 'yes' earns the point. U.S. processed meats (bacon, hot dogs, deli meat) named explicitly. IARC: processed meat Group 1, red meat Group 2A.

items.text: Do you have less than 1 serving a day of butter, margarine, or cream? (1 serving = 12 g, about 1 tablespoon.)
items.originalText: How many servings of butter, margarine, or cream do you consume per day? (1 serving: 12 g)
items.tip: Use olive oil on bread and vegetables instead of butter or margarine.
items.adaptationNote: Question reversed so 'yes' earns the point; 12 g described as about 1 tablespoon (1 tbsp butter = 14.2 g per USDA FDC). Note: DGA 2025-2030 lists butter among cooking fats; this item follows the Mediterranean/PREDIMED criterion and AHA 2021 (limit saturated fat).

items.text: Do you have less than 1 sweetened or carbonated soft drink a day (soda, sweet tea, energy or sports drinks, sweetened coffee drinks)?
items.originalText: How many sweet or carbonated beverages do you drink per day?
items.tip: Swap one soda or sweet drink a day for water, sparkling water, or unsweetened tea or coffee.
items.adaptationNote: Question reversed so 'yes' earns the point; U.S. drink examples added. App adaptation: plain unsweetened sparkling water is NOT counted (the original 'carbonated beverages' meant soft drinks; penalizing plain sparkling water would contradict DGA advice to choose water). Diet soft drinks still count, for fidelity with the original wording.

items.text: Do you drink 7 or more glasses of wine a week? (1 glass = 5 fl oz.)
items.originalText: How much wine do you drink per week?
items.tip: Nothing to change here. This question is kept only so the score matches the original screener. If you don't drink, you simply score 0 on it. Current guidance is that less alcohol is better for health.
items.adaptationNote: Kept for scoring fidelity only. The app must NEVER suggest starting or increasing drinking. Non-drinkers score 0 on this item, so their maximum is 13; compare scores over time, not against others. DGA 2025-2030: 'consume less alcohol for better overall health'; WHO 2023: no safe level. Evidence for a wine benefit is disputed (observational and confounded; Zhao 2023).

items.text: Do you eat 3 or more servings of beans, lentils, chickpeas, or split peas a week? (1 serving = 150 g cooked, about 3/4 cup; canned counts.)
items.originalText: How many servings of legumes do you consume per week? (1 serving: 150 g)
items.tip: Add a can of rinsed beans or chickpeas to a salad, soup or grain bowl, or batch-cook a pot of lentil soup.
items.adaptationNote: 150 g described as about 3/4 cup cooked (1 cup cooked lentils = 198 g per USDA FDC). Canned beans count; rinsing reduces sodium (FDA). Hummus is not named in the original; a large portion (≈150 g) may reasonably count, but this is an app interpretation.

items.text: Do you eat 3 or more servings of fish or shellfish a week? (1 serving = 100-150 g fish, about 3.5-5 oz, or 200 g shellfish; canned tuna, salmon and sardines count.)
items.originalText: How many servings of fish or shellfish do you consume per week? (1 serving: 100-150 g of fish or 4-5 units or 200 g of shellfish)
items.yesCriterion: Yes = ≥3 servings/week (1 serving = 100-150 g fish, or 4-5 pieces or 200 g shellfish).
items.tip: Canned fish makes this easy: sardines on whole-grain toast, or a tuna and bean salad.

alternativesIfAllergic.fish: If you avoid fish, beans/lentils, eggs and poultry are the protein swaps; you will score 0 on this item, which is fine. Plant omega-3 sources: walnuts, ground flaxseed.
alternativesIfAllergic.shellfish: Choose finned fish (salmon, sardines, tuna, cod) instead of shrimp or mussels.

items.adaptationNote: U.S. canned fish named; the MEDAS threshold (≥3/week) is higher than FDA/EPA advice (2+ servings/week of lower-mercury fish).

items.text: Do you eat store-bought sweets or pastries (cookies, cakes, donuts, pastries, snack cakes) fewer than 3 times a week?

items.tip: Try fruit, yogurt with honey, or a square of dark chocolate in place of one packaged sweet this week.
items.adaptationNote: Question reversed so 'yes' earns the point; U.S. examples (donuts, snack cakes) added. 'Biscuits' in the original means sweet biscuits/cookies, not U.S. savory biscuits.

items.text: Do you eat 3 or more servings of nuts (including peanuts) a week? (1 serving = 30 g, about a small handful or 1 oz.)
items.originalText: How many servings of nuts (including peanuts) do you consume per week? (1 serving: 30 g)
items.tip: Keep a small bag of unsalted nuts or trail mix in your pack or desk drawer.

alternativesIfAllergic.tree-nuts: Peanuts count in the original screener; or use seeds (sunflower, pumpkin) for a similar snack, though seeds don't count toward this item.
alternativesIfAllergic.peanuts: Use tree nuts (almonds, walnuts, pistachios) if tolerated, or seeds; seeds don't count toward this item.
alternativesIfAllergic.tree-nuts+peanuts: Seeds (sunflower, pumpkin) or ground flaxseed make a similar snack; they don't count toward this item, and scoring 0 here is fine.

items.adaptationNote: 30 g described as about 1 oz. App interpretation (not in the original): 2 tablespoons of natural peanut or nut butter may count as a serving. PREDIMED nut arm used 30 g/day mixed nuts.

items.text: Do you usually choose chicken or turkey instead of beef, pork, burgers, hot dogs or sausage?
items.originalText: Do you preferentially consume chicken, turkey, or rabbit meat instead of veal, pork, hamburger, or sausage?
items.yesCriterion: Yes = preferentially eats chicken, turkey or rabbit instead of veal, pork, hamburger or sausage.
items.tip: When you'd usually pick a burger or sausage, try chicken, turkey or fish.
items.adaptationNote: Rabbit and veal dropped as uncommon in the U.S.; beef and hot dogs added. The original gives no instruction for people who eat no meat; app interpretation: someone who eats no red meat can answer 'yes'.

items.short: Tomato-olive oil sauce dishes 2+ times a week
items.text: Do you eat dishes made with a tomato sauce cooked in olive oil with onion, garlic or leek (like homemade marinara, shakshuka, or tomato-based stews) 2 or more times a week?
items.originalText: How many times per week do you consume vegetables, pasta, rice, or other dishes seasoned with sofrito (sauce made with tomato and onion, leek, or garlic and simmered with olive oil)?
items.tip: Simmer canned tomatoes with olive oil and garlic or onion for 10 minutes, and use it on pasta, beans, eggs or fish.
items.adaptationNote: 'Sofrito' (a Spanish base sauce) described in U.S. terms. A jarred tomato sauce counts only if it is made with olive oil plus onion/garlic, or if you cook it with them (app interpretation; check the label).
